newsitem.title: USA: NYC Hevesi sees $200 mln of risks in FY '97 budget.
newsitem.headline: NYC Hevesi sees $200 mln of risks in FY '97 budget.

text.p: New York City Comptroller Alan Hevesi, who on Tuesday predicted that the city could have a $300 million budget surplus in the 1997 fiscal year, cautioned that there still are $200 million of risks in the budget.
But he added these risks are balanced by $538 million to $543 million of additional resources that have yet to be recognized.

Hevesi, in a report, said that the city's capital budget for fiscal year 1997 faces $777 million of risks in part because the Wicks Law, which obliges localities to split up construction contracts, has not been repealed.

And the state legislature has yet to act on the Giuliani Administration's proposal for a new infrastructure finance authority, which would be used to sidestep the constitutional ceiling on how much debt New York City can issue.

The comptroller noted that the Giuliani Administration's capital budget still includes $607 million from the sale of the city's water and sewer system, a proposal Hevesi has blocked in a court battle that is not expected to be resolved until early next year.
Achieving the projected budget surplus of over $300 million hinges on Wall Street's strong rebound, which has fattened the city's tax coffers, he added.
